title: Finite-Field Weil Input for p-adic Lattice Models
body_html:
Finite-Field Weil Input for p-adic Lattice Models

In the generalized lattice model for the p-adic oscillator representation, a building point \(z\) or a pair \((x,x')\) determines a lattice \(L=\mathcal{B}_{z,0}\) with symplectic annihilator \(L^{\perp_\psi}\subseteq L\). The quotient \[ \ell_L=L/L^{\perp_\psi} \] is a finite symplectic space, and the fiber of the lattice model is the finite Heisenberg representation attached to \(\ell_L\).

The stabilizer \(K_L\) of \(L\) acts on this fiber through the finite quotient \[ K_L/K_L^+\simeq \operatorname{Sp}(\ell_L). \] Thus Gérardin's finite-field Weil representation supplies the finite quotient action used in the p-adic lattice model.

The tensor-product facts for finite Weil representations are used after the lattice quotient decomposes as an orthogonal direct sum. In the theta-correspondence induction, this is the finite-level input behind the decomposition into diagonal brick factors and cross-term factors.

Finite-field character formulas should only be applied in the p-adic argument after passing to the quotient \(L/L^{\perp_\psi}\) and identifying the relevant stabilizer action with a finite reductive quotient. They do not by themselves prove any statement about the full p-adic stabilizer or the metaplectic splitting.
